docs.summary: Orbitly here is an independently maintained continuation of wheresfrank/openfamily (AGPL-3.0). It started from that project's history, which is preserved in this repository, and has since diverged…
docs.text: Relationship to the original project Orbitly here is an independently maintained continuation of wheresfrank/openfamily (AGPL-3.0). It started from that project's history, which is preserved in this repository, and has since diverged substantially. Nothing depends on upstream No git remote, workflow, updater, container image, release asset or APK download in this repository points at the original repository. The in-app and server update paths use this repository's own signed releases. The old Docker-socket updater was removed. There is no automatic synchronization. Do not enable "Sync fork". Reviewing upstream changes by hand (optional) git remote add upstream https://github.com/wheresfrank/openfamily.git git fetch upstream git log --oneline main..upstream/main # what they changed git diff main...upstream/main -- path/ # inspect before porting anything git cherry-pick <sha> # port a single fix if you want it git remote remove upstream # when done Port changes deliberately and test them. Keep the AGPL notices and the NOTICE attribution intact when copying code.

docs.title: Performance
docs.summary: The server is not the bottleneck (/healthz ~1.5 ms locally, hot endpoints below 15 ms p95 on a seeded database; see "Backend"). The work here targets the phone: rebuild cost, startup, and request…

headings.text: Before / after (measured in tests, same harness on `main` and here)

docs.text: Performance The server is not the bottleneck (/healthz ~1.5 ms locally, hot endpoints below 15 ms p95 on a seeded database; see "Backend"). The work here targets the phone: rebuild cost, startup, and request count. None of it could be run on a device while writing it, so this page also describes how to collect real numbers. On-device instrumentation Open Settings, tap the "Orbitly / Version" row 7 times (each tap within 2 s of the last). The hidden Performance screen shows: startup: process start to first frame (process age at main() from /proc/self/stat, plus main() to first frame) and timed startup steps; frame build and raster p50 / p90 / p99, janky-frame percentage against the display refresh rate (16.7 ms at 60 Hz, 8.3 ms at 120 Hz), and the 10 slowest frames with the screen that was visible (AppShell:location, a page class name, ...); per-screen rebuild counters (MapScreen, LocationTabView, PeopleList, PersonRow, MapMarkers, MapMarkerLayer); WebSocket frames received / applied / UI updates, total and per minute; HTTP requests and latency by endpoint (ring buffer of the last 400). Copy report puts a compact text report on the clipboard; Reset clears the counters. Only a tiny always-on frame summary runs by default (one FrameTiming callback, fixed-size histograms). Rebuilds, HTTP and WebSocket recorders are off until "Record details" is switched on. Everything is in memory: nothing is written to disk or sent anywhere. HTTP entries are METHOD /normalised/path only: ids, tokens, queries, bodies and coordinates never reach the buffer (path segments that are not plain lower-case words become :id). Code: app/lib/services/perf/perfmonitor.dart, app/lib/screens/performancescreen.dart. Collecting numbers 1. Install a release or profile build, open the Performance screen, switch on "Record details", Reset, then use the app for a few minutes (open the map, drag the sheet, switch tabs, open a trip report, let a family member drive). 2. Copy report and send it. 3. Cross-checks without the app: adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo app.openfamily reset then use the app, then adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo app.openfamily framestats (per-frame timestamps; "Janky frames" and the 50/90/95/99th percentiles are at the top of plain dumpsys gfxinfo app.openfamily). Cold start: adb shell am start -W -n app.openfamily/.MainActivity (TotalTime). Flutter DevTools: flutter run --profile, open the Performance tab (frame chart, "Track widget rebuilds"), the CPU profiler, and the Network tab. Use a profile build, never debug, for timings. What changed Area Change Map / sheet A WebSocket location frame no longer rebuilds MapScreen, the tab view, the tile layer or the sheet. The roster is a ValueNotifier that only the range circles, the marker layer and the People list listen to. Hidden tabs and covered routes skip those rebuilds (VisibleValueBuilder, keyed on TickerMode). Burst coalescing FamilyService delivers live frames to the UI at most once per 220 ms (leading edge immediate, trailing delivery with the newest data). Snapshots (REST, members frame, circle switch) are never delayed. Markers Bubble widgets are cached per member instance, so panning only recomputes positions. Tile layer sits in its own RepaintBoundary and is a const widget. People rows A row widget is reused while its member and flags are unchanged. Floating buttons The Check in / SOS / layers row is a ValueListenableBuilder child, not rebuilt on every sheet drag frame. Avatars Decoded at 2x display size with ResizeImage (was native size); a cached photo is in the first frame (no initials flash); decode is precached when the bytes land. Shell Tab bodies are created once; switching tabs no longer rebuilds every visited tab. Startup main() reads theme, map style and server URL in parallel and does not await the system-UI call. The session gate runs housekeeping, the /config fetch and the session check together. Push sync and the config refresh start after the first frame. Network /config cached 5 min and single-flighted; places cached 30 s (invalidated on create / update / delete / login / logout, bypassed by the Places screen); roster and places fetched side by side; family name and roster fetched together; the circles screen return no longer fetches /circles twice. JSON Responses of 128 KB or more are decoded with compute(). WebSocket Backoff resets only after a connection survived 10 s (was: on the first frame, so accept-then-drop servers were retried every second); connectivity events are debounced 800 ms. Audited and left alone: saveLayer sources (no BackdropFilter, ShaderMask, ColorFiltered, ImageFiltered or antiAliasWithSaveLayer anywhere; five Opacity / AnimatedOpacity uses that only layer while dimmed or fading, guarded by test/perf/savelayeraudittest.dart); no shrinkWrap lists; long lists are already lazy; no per-second tickers (labels are clock times); the vector tile layer stays mounted (dropping it would blank the map on every return to the Location tab, and while hidden it does no work now) with its existing 2 concurrent / 10 MB / 50 MB settings and a style future that is only recreated when the style URL changes. Considered and not done: showing the shell before the session check finishes. The check refreshes the token over the network when the 15-minute access token expired; running that in parallel with the first API calls would race two refreshes on the same refresh token. It needs the gate's refresh and the 401 refresh unified into one single-flight first. Behaviour changes /config is reused for 5 minutes (was refetched on resume); places for 30 s outside the Places screen. Live location frames reach the map at most ~4.5 times per second. The Driving / Circle tabs still update only on roster snapshots, exactly as before (the shared notifier keeps its identity semantics). WebSocket backoff reset and connectivity debounce, as above. Session gate: legacy cleanup no longer precedes the config fetch and session check (they run concurrently). Before / after (measured in tests, same harness on main and here) Proxy Before After Requests at startup (gate + map + push) 7 (/config x3) 5 Requests on resume / pull-to-refresh 3 (members, places, config) 1 Requests on circle switch 2 1 20 location frames: tab view rebuilds 20 0 20 location frames: person rows rebuilt 200 20 20 location frames: DsListRow builds 220 40 50 frames in 1 s: UI updates 50 6 20 tab switches (4 tabs visited): body rebuilds 80 0 30 pan frames, 6 members: bubble rebuilds 90 0 40 sheet-drag frames: floating buttons rebuilt 80 0 4000x3000 avatar at 44 dp, 3x: decoded bitmap 46,875 KB 204 KB 2.5 MB JSON: longest event-loop gap 76 ms (sync decode) 55 ms Hidden Location tab, 20 frames: row rebuilds not measured on main (it had no hidden-tab guard) 0 The JSON row is a weak result on a loaded x86 host: the gap includes isolate start-up and result hand-over, so treat the benefit on a phone as unconfirmed until measured. The numbers come from flutter test output lines starting PERFMETRIC (see test/perf, test/services/startuprequeststest.dart). Frame times, startup time and jank percentage cannot be measured in tests; use the Performance screen. Backend backend/internal/handlers/perfendpointstest.go (opt-in: OFPERF=1 and TESTDATABASEURL, throwaway database only) seeds 3 users, 20,000 locations, 300 trips, 1,020 trip events and 5 places on TimescaleDB, then times each endpoint 40 times through the real handlers (handler plus Postgres, no network): Endpoint p50 p95 GET /config 0.01 ms 0.04 ms GET /family/members 2.6 ms 7.0 ms GET /family/places 1.0 ms 1.2 ms GET /trips (30 days, limit 200) 1.8 ms 3.1 ms GET /trips/report (week) 6.4 ms 9.4 ms GET /trips/report (month) 7.9 ms 13.7 ms GET /trips/{id} 1.6 ms 4.0 ms POST /locations 5.3 ms 10.6 ms Everything is far below 100 ms, so no index or migration was added. Measure on the phone See the checklist in the pull-request description; in short: cold start time, janky % and p99 while dragging the sheet and panning with 3+ members, rebuild counts and WebSocket UI updates per minute during a drive, and the HTTP table after launch and after switching circle.

docs.title: Real-server interop test of the processing lanes
docs.summary: scripts/e2e-lanes.sh proves that the real Dart phone code (app/lib/services/e2ee/, LanesService, PrivateRuntime, ApiClient) works against the real Go server in backend/, instead of only against the…
docs.text: Real-server interop test of the processing lanes scripts/e2e-lanes.sh proves that the real Dart phone code (app/lib/services/e2ee/, LanesService, PrivateRuntime, ApiClient) works against the real Go server in backend/, instead of only against the in-memory fake (app/test/support/fakee2eeserver.dart). Docker only. The script builds the server, e2ee-bridge and a tiny SQL probe (copied temporarily to backend/cmd/e2eprobe, removed again) in golang:1.27, starts a throwaway TimescaleDB (fsync=off) and the server (host network, ports E2EDBPORT=55433, E2EAPIPORT=18089), then runs flutter test test/e2erealserver/ in ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:stable. Containers have unique names and are removed at the end. Extra arguments are passed to flutter test. scripts/e2e-lanes.sh E2EREQUIRESIDECAR=1 scripts/e2e-lanes.sh # also fail while the sidecar predates lanes E2EBUILTIN=1 scripts/e2e-lanes.sh test/e2erealserver/builtine2etest.dart # no sidecar: the API is its own server device E2ERUN=dev E2EKEEP=1 scripts/e2e-lanes.sh # keep the stack between runs (development) Without E2EBASEURL (the normal flutter test) the suite is skipped. How the pieces fit: ApiClient insists on https and one token store, so the tests use a pretend https host that a zone-scoped http client rewrites to the real server and signs with the token of the phone the call belongs to. The Orbitly server's own device is the real e2ee-bridge binary (enroll --kind server, approved by the admin phone through approveLinkRequest, pinned by run). Plaintext at the server is checked in the database (locations, memberpositions) through the probe, and the server log is grepped for Cleo's coordinates by the script. Scenarios (app/test/e2erealserver/lanese2etest.dart): policy, lanes in use (Anna, Ben server; Cleo phone), the real sidecar, cross reading and badges, opt-out, requiredserver, an app without the lanes capability, and a circle key handed out as the server key. Encrypted chat scenario app/test/e2erealserver/chate2etest.dart runs in the same stack (scripts/e2e-lanes.sh test/e2erealserver/chate2etest.dart): three phones exchange sealed chat, edit, delete (author and admin, plus a member's forged edit/delete that must change nothing), a photo, a removed member, and a member in the server lane whose chat still goes on the phone line while the real sidecar runs. The database is searched for the message words (e2eeitems, chatmessages, auditlog, photo blobs) and the script greps the server log for them at the end. Plaintext send answers 409 chatencrypted. Offline scenario (server stopped mid-test) app/test/e2erealserver/offlinee2etest.dart (run it on its own: scripts/e2e-lanes.sh test/e2erealserver/offlinee2etest.dart) proves the store-and-forward path against the real server. The script runs a small control loop next to the tests (E2ECTLDIR, mounted at /ctl): the test writes stop or start to /ctl/request and the script stops or starts the API container, answering in /ctl/ack. Anna's phone sends a chat message, the server is stopped, and her phone keeps queuing three more messages, a check-in and an SOS (real refused connections, no fakes), failed flushes lose nothing, the queue is "killed" and re-read from storage, the server is started, and everything arrives once and in order. Replaying the same client ids (a lost answer) changes nothing: the database is queried for exactly one check-in, one SOS and the four messages in order. See docs/design/OFFLINERESILIENCE.md.

Known limits of the in-app tools (so you do not over-trust them)

docs.text: Physical-device test procedures Emulators cannot prove background tracking, doze behaviour, OEM battery killers or real GPS. This document is the procedure; results go in the table at the end. Status: procedures written; physical execution BLOCKED. No agent has access to physical phones. Every result row below is "not run" until a human fills it in. Nothing in this document is a measured result. Everything in the one-hour run sheet and in the in-app Diagnostics and Self-test screens was written and unit-tested without ever running on a real phone: if one of them misbehaves on your device, that is a bug to report, not a user error. Device matrix (minimum) ID Device class Why A1 Pixel (stock Android, current release) Reference behaviour A2 Samsung (One UI) Aggressive background limits A3 Xiaomi/Oppo/OnePlus (OEM killer) Auto-start / battery saver kills A4 Low-end Android Go-class device (<=3 GB RAM) Memory pressure I1 iPhone (current iOS) Only after iOS distribution exists (see ../design/IOSRELEASE.md) Record OS version, app version (Settings -> About), battery health, SIM/Wi-Fi. Preconditions Server reachable over HTTPS; two test accounts in one circle; admin web open to watch the live map. App installed from the release APK, signed in, all permissions granted ("Allow all the time" location, notifications, battery: unrestricted). Fully charged; screen timeout 30 s; note starting battery %. Procedures P1. Background tracking (foreground service) 1. Start tracking, lock the screen, leave the phone 60 min stationary. 2. Pass: points keep arriving (admin Devices page "last seen" < 5 min old at every check); no "tracking stopped" notification. P2. Killed-app recovery 1. Swipe the app from recents; wait 15 min while walking 200 m. 2. Pass: points resume without opening the app (or document the OEM setting needed). P3. Doze / idle 1. Stationary, screen off, unplugged, 8 h overnight. 2. Pass: gap between consecutive points <= the configured idle interval x 2 on A1; record gaps on A2/A3. P4. Reboot persistence 1. Reboot the phone; do not open the app; walk 5 min. 2. Pass: tracking resumes within 5 min of boot (or documented limitation). P5. Offline queue 1. Airplane mode for 30 min while moving; then reconnect. 2. Pass: queued points upload in order, no duplicates (compare point count with GPX from a reference app). P6. Accuracy 1. Walk a known 1 km loop with a reference GPS app running in parallel. 2. Pass: track within 25 m of reference 95% of the time; distance within 5%. P7. Geofence arrival/departure 1. Place a 150 m geofence; approach from 1 km, enter, leave. 2. Pass: enter and exit notification each arrive within 2 min of crossing. P8. SOS and check-in Trigger SOS on A1 with screen off; pass if the other account is notified within 30 s. Repeat on cellular only. P9. Battery cost 1. 100% battery, unplugged, normal use plus tracking for 8 h on each device; same with tracking off as the control. 2. Record battery drop attributable to Orbitly from Android Settings -> Battery (app usage %) and adb shell dumpsys batterystats --charged if available. 3. Pass: attributable drain <= 5% per 8 h of mixed use (proposed budget; adjust after first baseline). P10. Update path Install vN, then vN+1 over it via Obtainium; pass if tracking continues and no re-login is needed. One-hour run sheet (v0.11 to v0.19 features) For the owner, on real phones. Needs: two phones on the same server (call them Phone A = yours and Phone B = a family member or a spare; ideally A is Android and B a different brand), a laptop with the admin panel open, a second account in one circle, and about 60 minutes. Do the sections in order; the time boxes include waiting. Screenshot anything marked [shot] and note the result in the template at the end. A step that cannot be done (feature not configured, no second phone) is recorded as SKIP with the reason, never as PASS. Conventions: "A:" means do it on Phone A, "B:" on Phone B, "Web:" in the admin panel. Menu names are the ones in app version 0.19.0; if a label differs slightly, find the nearest one and note it. Before you start (3 min) 1. A: Settings, tap the Orbitly version row (note the version), then Settings, Diagnostics. Expected: the checks load within about 10 seconds and the top banner says either "Everything looks right" or lists problems. [shot] 2. Fix every red item the screen lists (one tap each) until the banner is green, then Copy diagnostic report and paste it into your notes. Check the pasted text contains no coordinates, no token and no e-mail address. 3. Repeat on B. 4. Web: open Fleet health. Expected: both phones listed, each with app version, OS and "Self-report ... ago". [shot] If a phone shows "Not reported" for battery and permissions, it is running an older build; update it. 1. Diagnostics and self-test (8 min) 1. A: Diagnostics, Self-test, Run self-test. Expected, in order: Keystore PASS (shows "TEE" or "StrongBox"; "Software" is a finding to note), Vault PASS, Private circle encryption PASS, Upload PASS ("server registered it just now"), Notifications PASS with a Confirm chip, and you must see two notifications ("local test" and "Orbitly test alert") within 30 seconds. Only one or none: FAIL and note which. [shot] 2. A: Start background test, lock the phone, put it in your pocket and walk or sit five minutes with the screen off, then unlock and reopen the Self-test screen. Expected: "Background reporting works". FAIL means the OEM is killing the app: go back to Diagnostics and follow the battery advice for your brand, then repeat. 3. A, deliberately break it: Android Settings, Apps, Orbitly, Permissions, Location, choose Allow only while using the app. Reopen Diagnostics. Expected: a red "Location permission" card whose button opens the permission page; restore Allow all the time and the card turns green on return. Then Settings, Battery, set Orbitly to Optimized. Expected: an orange battery card (with a brand-specific button on Samsung, Xiaomi, OnePlus, Huawei, Oppo); restore Unrestricted. 4. A: set the phone clock manually 10 minutes wrong (turn off automatic time). Expected: Diagnostics shows a clock warning or failure. Turn automatic time back on. 5. A: airplane mode on, reopen Diagnostics. Expected: "Internet connection" red, server check "info" not red. Airplane mode off. 2. Silent-phone alert (7 min, includes waiting) 1. A (a circle admin): Settings, Notification settings, Silent phone alerts: set your circle to 4 hours (the shortest choice that is not "Off" for the first test is fine; the server default is Off). B: leave the setting alone. 2. The alert needs a few days of history to know B's normal hours, so on a fresh install this will not fire. Real test: pick a phone that has been reporting for 3+ days, switch it to airplane mode (or power it off) and wait for the threshold plus about 10 minutes. Expected: A (admin) gets "Phone hasn't checked in ... about N hours" and B gets "Orbitly can't reach your phone" when back online, opening the Diagnostics screen when tapped. The text must NOT contain a place or coordinates. With "Show names in notifications" off it says "A family member's phone". 3. Expected non-events: the same silence produces one alert, not repeats; nothing during the recipient's quiet hours (Settings, Notification settings, quiet hours); B turning on "Don't alert about my phone" stops it. 4. Record honestly if you could not wait: SKIP (needs 3 days of history plus a multi-hour wait). 3. Late-arrival alert (needs weeks of history, 2 min to set up) 1. A: Settings, Notification settings, Late-arrival alerts, switch on one saved place (only circles that are not Private show places here). Expected: the section exists and the toggle sticks after leaving and returning. 2. The alert itself needs at least 5 similar arrivals over 6 weeks. Record SKIP unless the place has that history; if it does, be late on a weekday and expect one alert to your circle about an hour after your usual time, at most two per day. 3. Private circles must not list places here at all. Record whether that held. 4. Invite page and joining (5 min) 1. A: open the circle and tap the invite card (or Circles, invite). Copy the link. 2. B (or any phone without the app): open the link in the browser. Expected: the invite page with install steps, a public APK download and a QR code, served without login. [shot] 3. B with the app installed: open the same link. Expected: the app opens straight into the join screen with the code filled in. Join. A sees B appear on the map within a minute. 5. Names in push, units, person panel (6 min) 1. A: Settings, Notification settings, Show names in notifications OFF. B: arrive at or leave a saved place (or use SOS-free Check In). Expected on A: "A family member ...". Turn it ON on A, repeat: "<First name> ...". Names must appear only for the recipient who opted in; B's setting must not change what A sees. 2. A: Settings, units tile: Miles to Kilometers. Expected: the Places radius list, speeds, the Driving tab, the weekly summary text and server-written notifications switch units, and the choice survives restarting the app. [shot] of one screen in each unit. 3. A: tap B on the map and again in the member list. Expected: the person panel opens (name, place presence, battery, speed, history/driving entries), no crash, back closes it. [shot] 6. Driving tab and phone-use detection (5 min; passenger only) Never operate a phone while driving. The driver keeps their eyes on the road; a passenger runs this. 1. A: Settings, Driving detection: switch on hard braking/acceleration and Detect phone use while driving (opt-in, off by default). 2. Take a short drive (10 minutes is enough) with A in the car. The passenger turns the screen on and off a few times mid-drive. 3. Afterwards: Driving tab. Expected: the trip appears with distance and duration in your chosen unit, event chips (brakes, speed), and a phone-use event for the screen-on moments, which you can mark passenger or dismiss. Record whether the events match what happened. 4. The Sunday weekly summary (Sunday 18:00 UTC) cannot be forced; record SKIP unless it arrives. 7. Place search (3 min) 1. A: Places, add a place, type the first letters of a street near you. Expected: suggestions appear within about 2 seconds, local results first, picking one drops the pin in the right place. Try a street in another country: results must not be forced to your region only when you type the full address. Note the language of the results. 8. Passkeys (2 min) As of v0.18.0 the server side exists (docs/passkeys.md) but no phone or web screen enrols or uses a passkey yet. Expected: no passkey option anywhere, and password sign-in still works on both phones and the web. Record N/A (no client UI) otherwise. Do not mark passkeys PASS. 9. Private circles (14 min) Use a throwaway circle, not your family's. 1. A: create a circle and turn on end-to-end encryption (Circle settings, Private/Encryption). Write down the recovery phrase on paper. Expected: the circle shows "End-to-end encrypted". 2. B: join it. A: approve B's key (compare the safety number or digits on both screens). Expected: B appears on A's map only after approval; the Diagnostics screen on both shows Private circle keys passing (info text about the lock screen is normal). 3. Lock both phones 5 minutes while moving. Unlock. Expected: positions appear on the other phone within about a minute of unlocking. Positions taken while locked are delivered late, by design. [shot] 4. Web: Admin panel, Fleet health: B's row says "Private circle" and shows timestamps only. Web, Encryption keys: both phone keys listed. The admin map must show no position for the circle. 5. Web viewer. Web: Private circles, create a viewer, choose storage mode "session". Copy the request code. A: the circle's settings, Approve a viewer or bridge, paste, compare name, fingerprint and digits, approve, copy the approval code back into the web page. Expected: the web map shows both members. Revoke the viewer from the phone afterwards and confirm it stops updating after the next key change. [shot] 6. Bridge. Needs a Dawarich and a machine that is NOT the server (backend/cmd/e2ee-bridge/README.md): run enroll, approve on A, run. Expected: points appear in Dawarich with no coordinates in the bridge log. Record SKIP if you have no Dawarich. 7. Trusted server. Only if you want the server to read the circle. A: Private circle, Trusted server, read the warning, consent; B must consent as well. Expected: the circle is labelled "Server can read (trusted server)", the admin map shows it, and withdrawing consent on either phone returns it to unreadable. Record SKIP if the e2ee-server sidecar is not deployed. [shot] 10. Dawarich export (4 min) Web: Settings, Dawarich card: URL, API key, enable. Expected: points from a plain (non-Private) circle arrive in Dawarich within a few minutes, once each; a Private circle contributes nothing (unless trusted-server mode or the bridge is on). Disabling stops new points but does not delete what was sent. Record SKIP without a Dawarich. Wrap up (2 min) 1. Web: Fleet health again. Expected: both phones healthy or with findings you already know about. [shot] 2. A and B: Diagnostics, Copy diagnostic report; attach both reports to your results. 3. Fill in the results table below. Note OS version, phone model, app version and server version at the top. What to screenshot (checklist) Diagnostics (green and with a red item), Self-test results, the invite page, one screen per unit system, the person panel, the Driving tab trip, Private circle map on both phones, the web viewer map, the Trusted-server label, Fleet health (before and after). Results template Copy into an issue or your notes. Result is one of PASS, FAIL, SKIP, N/A. docs.title: Orbitly app design system
docs.summary: Small, code-first. Everything lives in app/lib/theme and app/lib/widgets/ds. Import theme/apptheme.dart (tokens are re-exported) and widgets/ds/ds.dart.
docs.text: Orbitly app design system Small, code-first. Everything lives in app/lib/theme and app/lib/widgets/ds. Import theme/apptheme.dart (tokens are re-exported) and widgets/ds/ds.dart. Identity Light is Ice: lime on blue-grey paper. Dark is Night: brighter lime on charcoal. Lime is the action colour (buttons, selected states, pins), never a page wash. Colours come from AppColors and the BrandTheme extension (BrandTheme.of(context): paper, sheet, accent, accentInk, onAccent). Use accentInk when lime is a glyph or label on paper (it is AA-dark on Ice, bright on Night). Compat aliases (AppColors.purple, etc.) remain so older screens compile; new code should not use them. Tokens (theme/tokens.dart) Group Values AppSpace xxs 2, xs 4, sm 8, md 12, lg 16, xl 20, xxl 24, xxxl 32 AppRadius sm 8, md 12, lg 16, xl 24 (sheet top), pill AppType title 22/800, headline 17/700, body 15/600, secondary 13/500, label 12/700 caps AppMotion fast 150ms, normal 250ms; AppMotion.of(context, d) returns zero when the OS disables animations kMinTarget 48dp minimum interactive size Rules: no hard-coded spacing or radii in new code; no fixed-height boxes around text (text scales to 200%); colour never carries meaning alone (every chip and row has a text label); every tap target is at least 48dp; every icon-only control has a tooltip/semantic label. Widgets (widgets/ds) Widget Use DsPillButton Stadium button: filled (lime), tonal, outlined, danger (SOS). Optional icon. DsMapButton 48dp round floating control over the map (settings, layers, locate). Tooltip is its label. Optional attention badge. DsSectionHeader Small-caps group label, marked as a semantic header. DsListRow Avatar/icon, title, status line, trailing, optional chevron; selected, destructive; DsListRow.iconTile for settings icons. DsToggleRow Row with a Switch; the whole row toggles; exposes toggled semantics; null onChanged disables. DsSheetScaffold / DsDragHandle Rounded sheet surface with handle and optional title/header. DsSegmentedTabs Equal-width pill tabs (People / Places). DsStatusChip One glanceable fact ("Battery 18%"). DsEmptyState, DsErrorState, DsOfflineBanner Calm, illustration-free states with an optional action. DsErrorState takes an icon (cloud-off for offline). DsPage Form / onboarding page: app bar (+ step indicator), readable-width scrolling body, pinned actions. At text larger than 140% the actions scroll with the content. DsHeading Page title + calm supporting line (semantic header). DsMessage Inline error / success / info with icon AND words, live region. DsOptionCard Big tappable choice (create / join). One semantic button. DsBusyButton DsPillButton that swaps to "Please wait" while busy. DsSkeleton, DsSkeletonList Loading placeholders; static when the OS removes animations. showDsConfirm Confirm dialog. destructive: true adds a warning icon and the danger pill; buttons stack and the body scrolls at large text. Use for delete account, log out everywhere, remove member. DsRowGroup Rounded card of DsListRows with dividers, for use inside DsPage. DsChoiceSetting Pick one of a few values (theme, map style, units): segmented control, or check-marked rows at text over 130%. OnboardingStepIndicator "Step X of Y" with segments, used as DsPage(step:, totalSteps:). App shell AppShell (screens/appshell.dart) hosts four lazily-built, state-keeping tabs in an IndexedStack under a Material 3 NavigationBar: 1. Location - MapScreen rendering LocationTabView: full-bleed map, settings button, circle pill (switcher), invite button, Check in / SOS pills, layers and locate buttons, and a draggable People / Places sheet. The map widget is a black box passed to LocationTabView, so the tile layer can change without touching the layout. 2. Driving - who is driving now; each row opens TripsScreen. 3. Safety - SOS, check in, help alert, alert history, emergency contacts. 4. Circle - profile, circles, invite, places, security, settings. Back on any tab other than Location returns to Location; back on Location leaves the app. Routes pushed on the root navigator (alert screens, SOS) cover the bar. AppShell.requestTab(AppTab.safety) switches tabs from non-widget code (works before the shell mounts). There is deliberately no chat button; LocationTabView has a marked slot top-right for it. Testing test/widgets/dswidgetstest.dart, locationtabviewtest.dart, test/screens/appshelltest.dart use test/support/locationfixtures.dart (fake members, circles, places, a drawn stand-in map). Golden renders: OFGOLDENS=1 flutter test --update-goldens test/goldens writes test/goldens/.png (Roboto loaded from the SDK). They are skipped unless OFGOLDENS=1, so a normal flutter test does not compare pixels. Second wave (onboarding, auth, family, security) Welcome (three value-prop pages), sign up, sign in (with the two-factor / recovery-code step), reset password, create-or-join, create family, join, invite, permissions (location Always, notifications, motion, Android battery optimization), family, profile, circles, circle detail / create and the security screens all use DsPage, themed inputs (inputDecorationTheme: filled sheet colour, 12dp radius, accentInk focus ring) and the shared states. securitywidgets.dart keeps its names (BusyButton, ErrorText, LoadStateView, Callout) but renders with the design system. The invite screen leaves a keyed empty slot (invite-qr-slot) between the code and the actions for the QR code / join link of issue #40. Goldens for these screens live in test/goldens/r2.png (light, dark, and 200% text for welcome, sign in and permissions). Third wave (safety, alerts, trips, places) SOS, check in, help alert, alert status / received / history, safety (emergency contacts), trips, trip detail, driving report, day detail, places and the place picker use the same tokens, DsPillButton, DsListRow, DsStatusChip and the shared states. SOS rules that every change must keep: Honest wording: "Your family was notified. Emergency services were NOT contacted." (kFamilyNotifiedLine) is shown on every sent alert, and the SOS screen says up front that SOS does not call emergency services. Delivery states are an icon plus words (deliveryStateStyle), never colour alone. AlertTile shows Active / Resolved as a DsStatusChip with an icon. The regional emergency dial button (EmergencyCallButton) opens the phone's dialler with the local number; it never places the call by itself. No coordinates in notification text. (The place picker shows the pin's coordinates on screen only, as a pin-drop aid.) Slide-to-cancel always has a plain Cancel button next to it. Screens scroll instead of squeezing at large text; the SOS disc is 200dp. Trips and the driving report keep the "GPS speed" labelling and the mph / km/h conversion (UnitSystem). PlacesScreen takes an optional loader for tests and goldens. Location tab: the circle pill shows "Location sharing: on / paused" and opens the circle sheet. Every circle row has an info button ("Open details for X") and, for the selected circle, the sheet header has "Open circle details" and a sharing chip. Selecting a row still only selects it. Goldens: test/goldens/m3.png (SOS, alert status, trips, report, places in light, dark and 200% text). Third wave (account, people, settings) Change password, delete account, sessions, two-factor, issue reset code, member edit / profile, people, profile, server, privacy, add locations, settings and the circles screens now share the same page, row-group, confirm and state widgets. SecurityPage is a DsPage; BusyButton renders DsBusyButton (danger = the system's danger pill). The Material 3 FAB is flat (floatingActionButtonTheme elevation 0): its default black shadow showed as a black ring around the lime button on Night. Goldens: test/goldens/acct.png (light, dark and 200% text), from test/goldens/accountgoldentest.dart.

docs.title: Large screens and Android system UI
docs.summary: The app draws edge to edge (SystemChrome edgeToEdge in main.dart, WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) in MainActivity; Android 15+ enforces it anyway). Every screen must therefore pad…
docs.text: Large screens and Android system UI The app draws edge to edge (SystemChrome edgeToEdge in main.dart, WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) in MainActivity; Android 15+ enforces it anyway). Every screen must therefore pad itself from MediaQuery insets, never from an assumed status-bar height. Rules System bars are transparent; icon brightness follows the app theme (systemOverlayFor in theme/apptheme.dart), applied in MaterialApp.builder and in AppBarTheme. App bars handle the status bar. Bodies use Scaffold + DsBody (safe left, right, bottom; centered at kContentMaxWidth = 640 dp) or DsPage (560 dp). The bottom NavigationBar already insets for the gesture bar. Full-screen map overlays add MediaQuery.paddingOf(context).bottom themselves. Pinned actions go outside the scroll view so the keyboard (viewInsets) never hides them (place picker, DsPage). Cutout: windowLayoutInDisplayCutoutMode=shortEdges (values-v28 and up). Predictive back: android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true"; back handling is PopScope (AppShell returns to Location first). Breakpoints Width / orientation Layout <= 412 dp portrait unchanged phone layout 480 dp (S26 Ultra class) phone layout, compact 2x2 driving tiles = 520 dp content four driving tiles across = 840 dp, or landscape >= 560 dp NavigationRail instead of bottom bar; Location is map + side panel (no sheet); place picker is map + form content cap 560 (forms), 640 (lists/settings), 760 (detail with maps) Verifying test/support/goldenutils.dart applies a DeviceSpec (size, status bar, cutout, gesture bar, keyboard, text scale) to the test view and paints fake system chrome. test/widgets/insetstest.dart asserts the inset rules. Goldens: OFGOLDENS=1 flutter test --update-goldens test/goldens/lsgoldentest.dart (files test/goldens/ls). Not covered: real device behaviour.

docs.text: Life360 flow analysis (reference study for the redesign) Issue: #28. Method and limits, stated honestly: the Life360 web pages were not fetched or scraped, and no Life360 assets, copy, icons or screenshots are used here. This is written from (a) widely documented public product behaviour (app-store listings, help-centre-level knowledge, public reviews) as recalled, and (b) Orbitly's own screens in app/lib/screens. Life360 behaviour can have changed and is unverified against the live product. The issue's "15 Page Flows" list was not available in the issue text, so the 15 flows below are the standard journeys of this product category; the maintainer should confirm the intended list. Pages that need a paid Life360 account or an installed app (Gold/Platinum tiers, Driver Report details, Crash Detection settings) are marked inaccessible - not observed. Legend for the Orbitly column: Have (screen exists), Partial, Gap. Flow What Life360-style apps do (public behaviour) Orbitly today Status 1 Welcome / value pitch Short carousel, then Create account or Log in welcomescreen.dart, onboardingscreen.dart Have 2 Sign up Phone/email, name, password; permission education follows signupscreen.dart, invite-gated registration Have 3 Log in / reset Email or phone login; reset by link/code loginscreen.dart, resetpasswordscreen.dart, issueresetcodescreen.dart (operator-issued codes, no email) Have (differs by design) 4 Permission onboarding Staged location ("Always"), motion, notification, battery prompts with explanation permissionsscreen.dart, battery-optimization intent Have 5 Create or join a Circle Create with name; join by invite code or link; multiple circles createorjoincirclescreen.dart, circlecreatescreen.dart, joincirclescreen.dart, invitescreen.dart, multi-circle (docs/design/CIRCLES.md) Have 6 Main map Full-screen map, member bubbles with battery/status, bottom sheet of members mapscreen.dart, appshell.dart, docs/bubbles.md Have 7 Member detail Tap a member: address, last updated, battery, speed, history entry, check-in/ping memberdetailscreen.dart, memberprofilescreen.dart Have 8 Places / geofences Add places with radius; arrival/departure alerts per member placesscreen.dart, placepickerscreen.dart, addlocationsscreen.dart, placealertrulesscreen.dart Have 9 Location history Day list, route with stops; paid tiers extend the window dailyhistoryscreen.dart, daydetailscreen.dart, tripsscreen.dart, tripdetailscreen.dart Have (no paywall) 10 Driving safety Trip list, hard-braking/speeding/phone-use events, weekly score drivingtabscreen.dart, drivingreportscreen.dart, familydrivingreportscreen.dart, docs/driving.md Have (phone-use event: Gap) 11 Crash detection Detects a crash, countdown, contacts emergency services/contacts crashcountdownscreen.dart, crashreportsscreen.dart Have (professional dispatch: not offered) 12 SOS / Help alert One-tap alert to circle with location; paid tiers add dispatch sosscreen.dart, helpalertscreen.dart, alertreceivedscreen.dart, alertstatusscreen.dart, safetyhubscreen.dart Have 13 Check-in and chat "I'm here" check-in, circle messages checkinscreen.dart, chatscreen.dart, inboxscreen.dart, docs/chat.md Have 14 Settings, notifications, privacy Per-circle location sharing toggle, notification prefs, delete account, ghost/pause settingsscreen.dart, notificationprefsscreen.dart, securityscreen.dart, twofactorscreen.dart, sessionsscreen.dart, deleteaccountscreen.dart, privacypolicyscreen.dart Have 15 Membership / upsell Free/Gold/Platinum tiers, paywall for history length, Tile devices, ID theft protection - Intentionally absent (self-hosted, no tiers) Inaccessible - not observed: tier-specific screens (extended history, roadside assistance, ID-theft products, Tile hardware pairing), account-recovery edge cases, and any flow gated by a US phone number. Takeaways for the redesign Map-first shell with a draggable member sheet is the organising pattern; Orbitly already follows it (appshell.dart, mapscreen.dart). Remaining polish is in density of the member sheet and tablet layout (docs/ux/LARGESCREEN.md). Onboarding sequences permission education before the OS prompt and stages "Always" location after While-in-Use; keep this order (permissionsscreen.dart). Safety features are grouped in one hub; Orbitly's safetyhubscreen.dart matches. A visible "all clear" circle status is a possible addition. Gaps worth considering: phone-use-while-driving events, a pause/"ghost" mode surfaced next to the map (check against docs/safety.md), and a first-run checklist ("add a place", "invite someone"). No paywall, ads or data-sale flows exist or should be added; this is a privacy differentiator (PRIVACY.md). Do not copy Life360 trademarks, copy text, icons or imagery. Visual design stays governed by docs/ux/DESIGNSYSTEM.md.
